data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 asserts reliability gain comes from error cancellation (wisdom of the crowd) rather than the checklist, but its own countercondition (perfectly correlated non-expert errors) shows the mechanism is fragile. More importantly, the target fails to address the problem's required distinguishing evidence: within a single evaluation, if the panel's errors are correlated by the checklist itself (everyone misses the same case because the checklist omits it), the crowd mechanism cannot distinguish genuine gain from compliance, because the coordination device is also the source of shared bias. The target offers no within-evaluation evidence to separate the two.
